# Quick Start - Production Deployment

This guide gets you up and running with Colony v1.1.0 in production with all security and reliability features enabled.

## Prerequisites

- Kubernetes cluster (1.25+)
- Gateway API CRDs installed
- Namespaces created with proper labels
- Secrets prepared

---

## 1. Secrets (Auto-Generated by Default) ✨

### OAuth2 Client Secret - AUTO-GENERATED

**Good News:** OAuth2 secrets are **automatically generated** by default! The chart will create the secret for you if it doesn't exist.

**Secret Name:** `{serviceName}-oauth2-secret`  
**Example:** For `serviceName: myservice`, secret is `myservice-oauth2-secret`

**If you prefer to create manually:**

```bash
# Optional: Create OAuth2 secret manually
kubectl create secret generic myservice-oauth2-secret \
  -n core \
  --from-literal=client-secret='your-secure-oauth2-secret-here'

# Then disable auto-generation in values
oauth2:
  autoGenerateSecret: false
```

### Queue Secret (if using NATS)

```bash
# Create NATS queue secret
kubectl create secret generic queue-myservice-secret \
  -n core \
  --from-literal=username='myservice' \
  --from-literal=password='your-secure-nats-password' \
  --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -

# Add reflector annotations for datastore namespace
kubectl annotate secret queue-myservice-secret \
  -n core \
  reflector.v1.k8s.emberstack.com/reflection-allowed=true \
  reflector.v1.k8s.emberstack.com/reflection-allowed-namespaces=datastore \
  reflector.v1.k8s.emberstack.com/reflection-auto-enabled=true \
  reflector.v1.k8s.emberstack.com/reflection-auto-namespaces=datastore
```

---

## 2. Prepare Namespace Labels

```bash
# Label namespace for network policies
kubectl label namespace core \
  kubernetes.io/metadata.name=core

kubectl label namespace datastore \
  kubernetes.io/metadata.name=datastore

kubectl label namespace telemetry \
  kubernetes.io/metadata.name=telemetry

kubectl label namespace envoy-gateway-system \
  kubernetes.io/metadata.name=envoy-gateway-system

# Enable Pod Security Standards
kubectl label namespace core \
  pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=restricted \
  pod-security.kubernetes.io/audit=restricted \
  pod-security.kubernetes.io/warn=restricted
```

---

## 3. Create Values File

Create `values-myservice-prod.yaml`:

```yaml
serviceName: myservice
namespace: core

image:
  registry: ghcr.io
  repository: antinvestor/myservice
  tag: v1.0.0

# High availability
replicaCount: 3

# Enhanced security
securityContext:
  runAsUser: 1000
  runAsGroup: 1000
  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true  # If app supports

resources:
  limits:
    cpu: 1000m
    memory: 1Gi
  requests:
    cpu: 200m
    memory: 400Mi

# Gateway
gateway:
  enabled: true
  type: http  # or grpc
  hostname: myservice.chamamobile.com

# OAuth2 with auto-generation (SECURE & AUTOMATIC)
oauth2:
  enabled: true
  autoGenerateSecret: true  # Enabled by default - creates secret automatically!
  audience: "service_notifications"

# Network policy (IMPORTANT!)
networkPolicy:
  enabled: true

# Environment variables
env:
  # Database
  - name: DATABASE_USERNAME
    valueFrom:
      secretKeyRef:
        name: hub-core-app
        key: username
  - name: DATABASE_PASSWORD
    valueFrom:
      secretKeyRef:
        name: hub-core-app
        key: password
  - name: DATABASE_URL
    value: "postgres://$(DATABASE_USERNAME):$(DATABASE_PASSWORD)@pooler-rw.datastore.svc.cluster.local:5432/myservice"
  
  # Queue
  - name: QUEUE_USERNAME
    valueFrom:
      secretKeyRef:
        name: queue-myservice-secret
        key: username
  - name: QUEUE_PASSWORD
    valueFrom:
      secretKeyRef:
        name: queue-myservice-secret
        key: password
  - name: EVENTS_QUEUE_URL
    value: "nats://$(QUEUE_USERNAME):$(QUEUE_PASSWORD)@queue.datastore.svc.cluster.local:4222?subject=svc.myservice.internal._queue&consumer_durable_name=svc_myservice_internal_queue&stream_name=svc_myservice&stream_subjects=svc.myservice.%3E&consumer_ack_policy=explicit&jetstream=true"

# Volumes (if using readOnlyRootFilesystem)
volumes:
  - name: tmp
    emptyDir: {}
volumeMounts:
  - name: tmp
    mountPath: /tmp
```

---

## 4. Validate Configuration

```bash
# Dry-run to check for errors
helm install myservice ./charts/colony \
  -f values-myservice-prod.yaml \
  --dry-run --debug
```

---

## 5. Deploy

```bash
# Install
helm install myservice ./charts/colony \
  -f values-myservice-prod.yaml \
  -n core
```

---

## 6. Verify Deployment

```bash
# Check pods are running
kubectl get pods -n core -l app.kubernetes.io/name=myservice

# Check pod distribution (anti-affinity)
kubectl get pods -n core -l app.kubernetes.io/name=myservice -o wide
# Should see pods on different nodes

# Check PDB
kubectl get pdb -n core myservice

# Check network policy
kubectl get networkpolicy -n core myservice

# Check health
kubectl exec -n core deployment/myservice -- curl http://localhost:8080/healthz

# Check logs
kubectl logs -n core -l app.kubernetes.io/name=myservice --tail=50

# Check HPA
kubectl get hpa -n core myservice
```

---

## 7. Test External Access

```bash
# Test via gateway
curl https://myservice.chamamobile.com/healthz

# Should return 200 OK
```

---

## 8. Monitor

```bash
# Watch pod metrics
watch kubectl top pods -n core -l app.kubernetes.io/name=myservice

# Watch HPA
watch kubectl get hpa -n core myservice

# Check for events
kubectl get events -n core --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | grep myservice
```

---

## Default Configurations (Already Enabled)

The following security and reliability features are **enabled by default** in v1.1.0:

✅ **Pod Anti-Affinity** (preferred)
- Spreads pods across nodes automatically

✅ **Graceful Termination** (60s)
- Allows clean shutdown

✅ **PreStop Hook**
- 10s delay for load balancer de-registration

✅ **Improved PDB** (50%)
- Maintains at least 50% pods during disruptions

✅ **Security Context**
- Non-root execution
- Dropped capabilities
- SecComp profile

✅ **Health Probes**
- Startup, liveness, readiness

✅ **Auto-Scaling**
- HPA with CPU/memory targets

✅ **OpenTelemetry**
- Kubernetes metadata injection

---

## What You Must Enable

### Network Policies (Required for Production)

```yaml
networkPolicy:
  enabled: true  # MUST enable in production
```

### OAuth2 Secret Reference (Recommended)

```yaml
oauth2:
  clientSecretRef:
    name: myservice-oauth2-secret
    key: client-secret
```

---

## Production Checklist

Before going to production, ensure:

- [ ] OAuth2 secrets created and referenced (not inline)
- [ ] Queue secrets created (if using NATS)
- [ ] Database credentials secret exists
- [ ] Network policy enabled
- [ ] Namespace labels applied
- [ ] Resource limits profiled and set
- [ ] Gateway hostname configured
- [ ] External DNS configured (if used)
- [ ] Health probes tested
- [ ] Monitoring configured
- [ ] Alerts configured
- [ ] Tested in staging environment
- [ ] Rollback plan documented

---

## Common Issues

### Pods Pending

```bash
# Check pod events
kubectl describe pod -n core <pod-name>

# Common causes:
# - Insufficient resources
# - Anti-affinity constraints (not enough nodes)
# - Image pull errors

# Solution for anti-affinity:
podAntiAffinity:
  type: preferred  # Use preferred instead of required
```

### Network Policy Blocking Traffic

```bash
# Temporarily disable to test
networkPolicy:
  enabled: false

# Add specific allow rule
networkPolicy:
  additionalEgressRules:
    - to:
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: required-service
```

### Secret Not Found

```bash
# List secrets
kubectl get secrets -n core

# Create missing secret
kubectl create secret generic myservice-oauth2-secret \
  -n core \
  --from-literal=client-secret='your-secret'
```
